title: Shmup
blurb: A walkable first-person street block, ported line-for-line from the browser FPS Claude of Duty onto Axiom's deterministic engine core.
description: An in-progress, faithful port of the browser FPS at C:/dev/Claude-of-Duty (Three.js r180, ISC) onto Axiom. The deterministic core is ported module-for-module against the JavaScript source — the fixed-step engine loop, the movement state machine (walk/sprint/tactical-sprint/crouch/prone/slide/mantle/vault/lean), the spring-driven camera rig (bob, recoil, landing impact, breathing sway), procedurally generated street-block geometry (buildings, kerbs, pavements, alleys), and 19 procedural surface materials, lit by a ported atmosphere model at a fixed time of day. WASD to move, Shift to sprint (double-tap for tactical sprint), C to crouch, Z to prone, Space to jump, Q/E to lean, mouse to look (click to lock the pointer, Esc to release). What is honestly not wired up yet: there is no viewmodel rig or weapon firing (the rifle sits in the street as a placed object), no AI, no HUD damage/objectives, and no audio bridge — each is a real subsystem ported natively and unit-tested, just not yet connected to a renderable or interactive seam. (WebGPU, with a WebGL2 / Canvas2D fallback.)
